text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Nigerian pro-democracy groups in collaboration with Amnesty International plan demonstration on November 10 to mark first year anniversary of hanging of rights activist Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight associates, special duties minister Wada Nas says.
- Hope rises for possible crude oil find in northeastern Lake Chad Basin after 12-year search by state-owned Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation.
- Upgrading of Forcados crude oil loading terminal in the midwest by Shell Nigeria will now be completed in January 1998, 12 months behind schedule, officials say.
- Military ruler General Sani Abacha restates intention of army to hand power to an elected civilian by October 1998.

- Secrecy law is impeding effective implementation of standard banking principles in West and Central Africa, Central Bank governor Paul Ogwuma tells a sub-regional conference of banking supervisors in the capital Abuja.

- Solid expansion in agriculture and increased petroleum production will boost Nigeria's economy to record a 3.5 percent growth from this year from 2.2 percent last year, says report by a private group Economic Intelligence Unit.

- Hanged author Ken Saro-Wiwa's Movement for the Survival of Ogoni Peoples (MOSOP) assures government in a statement that it does not intend to stage any demonstration on November 10 but rather to mark the day quietly.
- National electoral commission chairman Sumner Dagogo-Jack has fixed November 11 to December 2 for compilation of new voters' register, sources say.

- Low capital base of Nigerian companies is responsible for their inability to compete effectively on the international business scene, S.O.Dada, president of the Chartered Institute of Bankers (CIBN) says.
